name: test_save_restore
prose: Test function taking idx (0 or 1 selects which save API is exercised); it manipulates the calling thread's OpenSSL error queue and returns 1 on success, 0 on the first failed check. It allocates an ERR_STATE with OSSL_ERR_STATE_new() (returns 0 if that fails), raises ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE and records ERR_peek_last_error() as mallocfail (returns 0 if that is not greater than 0), for idx == 1 sets a mark with ERR_set_mark() (returns 0 if it does not return 1), raises ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR with data "test data" and records its code as interr (returns 0 if it equals mallocfail). For idx == 0 it calls OSSL_ERR_STATE_save() and checks the queue is then empty (last error is 0); for idx == 1 it calls OSSL_ERR_STATE_save_to_mark(), which saves only the entries above the mark, and checks the queue is not empty (the marked malloc-failure entry stays). It then loops twice: OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore() appends the saved entries, the last error must equal interr with data "test data" and flags ERR_TXT_STRING | ERR_TXT_MALLOCED, a second restore duplicates the saved entries, and the queue is drained with ERR_get_error_all() checking each entry (for idx == 0 the saved set is mallocfail then interr, giving mallocfail, interr, mallocfail, interr; for idx == 1 the saved set is only interr, so the queue holds the still-queued mallocfail on the first iteration followed by interr twice, and only interr twice on the second iteration), ending with ERR_get_error() == 0. Any failed check jumps to err, leaving the queue as it is; OSSL_ERR_STATE_free(es) is called on every exit after es is declared (also when allocation failed, where es is NULL). Returns 1 only when all checks pass; success requires the queue to be empty on entry because of the final ERR_get_error() == 0 check.

Reviewer round 15 (idx==1 second restore duplicates only interr, not mallocfail) is right (lines 363,383-389,391-411); round 1 claim about idx==1 saving mallocfail is right too (save_to_mark at 363); round 2 (empty-queue precondition) mixed: stated in the old prose as a precondition for the final check at line 413, kept only as a remark. name: test_EVP_SM2
prose: Test function (no parameters, uses globals testctx and testpropq, and the message kMsg) that exercises SM2 keygen, sign/verify and encrypt/decrypt, returning 1 if every check passes and 0 at the first failure. It creates an SM2 EVP_PKEY_CTX, sets the sm2 curve with EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_ec_paramgen_curve_nid, generates parameters and then a key, creates two EVP_MD_CTX and an EVP_PKEY_CTX for the key shared by both digest contexts, and fetches "sm3". It signs kMsg with DigestSign after setting a 10-byte SM2 id with EVP_PKEY_CTX_set1_id, obtaining the signature size first and allocating the buffer with OPENSSL_malloc, then verifies it with the same id (must return > 0), then re-initialises the verify context and sets a zero-length id and requires DigestVerifyFinal to return exactly 0. It then loops over the digests "SM3" (the entry is NULL and skipped when OPENSSL_NO_SM3 is defined) and "SHA2-256": it frees any previous cctx, creates a new context, encrypts kMsg, decrypts, reads the digest name back, fetches that digest and requires EVP_MD_is_a to match the requested name, requires the decrypted length to equal sizeof(kMsg) and the bytes to equal kMsg. Any failed check goes to done; on every exit at done it frees pctx, kctx, sctx, cctx, the keys, both digest contexts, check_md and sig. Returns 1 only after the loop completes. If creating cctx fails on the second loop iteration, the pointer freed at the top of the loop is freed again at done (lines 2733, 2741-2743, 2796).

name: setup_tests
prose: Test-registration entry point (no parameters) that processes command-line options with opt_next() and then registers test cases with ADD_TEST / ADD_ALL_TESTS; it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. In the option loop, OPT_CONTEXT creates testctx with OSSL_LIB_CTX_new() (returns 0 if that gives NULL), when STATIC_LEGACY is defined adds the builtin legacy provider (returns 0 if that fails), and loads the "null" provider into the default context and "default" (and, unless OPENSSL_SYS_TANDEM, "legacy") into testctx without checking those load results; OPT_CONFIG_FILE stores opt_arg() and calls test_get_libctx(), returning 0 if it fails; OPT_TEST_CASES does nothing; any other option returns 0. If a config file was given it registers only test_EVP_set_config_properties and returns 1. Otherwise it registers the full set of tests, with many guarded by OPENSSL_NO_* macros; the engine tests (test_signatures_with_engine, test_cipher_with_engine) are registered only if OPENSSL_NO_DYNAMIC_ENGINE is not defined (and OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0 is not) and testctx is NULL. Under OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0 undefined it also creates custom_pmeth with EVP_PKEY_meth_new(0xdefaced, 0), setting its check callbacks and adding it with EVP_PKEY_meth_add0, returning 0 if the creation fails or add0 does not return 1. It returns 1 at the end. It assigns the globals testctx, nullprov, deflprov, lgcyprov and custom_pmeth.

name: rand_test_run
prose: EVP_TEST run callback for DRBG known-answer tests: it reads the parsed RAND_DATA from t->data, allocates got of generate_bits/8 bytes with OPENSSL_malloc (returns 0 if that fails), converts the init controls with ctrl2params when there are any (goto err if that fails, returning 0), and appends the use_df, cipher, digest and "HMAC" mac parameters before calling EVP_RAND_CTX_set_params on expected->ctx. If that set_params call fails, it jumps to err with ret = 1 and t->err = "EVP_RAND_CTX_set_params" when t->expect_unapproved is 0, or returns 0 (t->err untouched) when t->expect_unapproved is non-zero. Otherwise it loops over items 0..expected->n: it instantiates the parent and the ctx (with the test entropy, nonce and personalisation string), optionally sets reseed entropy on the parent and reseeds, optionally sets pr_entropyA/pr_entropyB on the parent, calls EVP_RAND_generate twice (additional inputs A then B), requires the output of the second generate to equal item->output, calls rand_check_fips_approved (returns 0 if the FIPS indicator query fails or check_fips_approved reports a mismatch with t->expect_unapproved), and uninstantiates ctx and parent, verifying zeroization and that the ctx state is EVP_RAND_STATE_UNINITIALISED. Each failed TEST_* check or step jumps to err with ret still 0 (t->err is not set on those paths). If all iterations pass, t->err = NULL and ret = 1. At err it prints the failing case index when i >= 0, frees got and the converted params, and returns ret.

name: test_mod_exp_x2
prose: Test function taking idx that selects the operand size: factor_size is 1024 for idx <= 100, 1536 for 101..200, 2048 for 201..300 and stays 0 for idx > 300 (no early return; the function continues with factor_size 0). It creates a BN_CTX and ten BIGNUMs (returns 0 if any allocation fails), fills a1, b1, a2, b2 with BN_rand and m1, m2 as odd random numbers (the return values of BN_rand are not checked), reduces a1, b1 mod m1 and a2, b2 mod m2 with BN_mod, computes two results with BN_mod_exp_simple and both at once with BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime_x2, and returns 0 if any of those calls does not succeed. It then compares each simple result with the matching x2 result; if either pair differs it prints diagnostics (TEST_info and BN_print_var of all values) and returns 0. It returns 1 when all calls succeeded and both results match. All BIGNUMs and the BN_CTX are freed at err on every return after the first allocation attempt.

name: fake_rsa_dgstvfy
prose: Fake provider one-shot digest-verify callback; ctx is treated as a pointer to a single flag byte and sig, siglen, tbv, tbvlen are not otherwise inspected. It first calls fake_rsa_dgstsgnvfy_update, which returns 0 if ctx is NULL, if the flag byte is 0, or if the FINALISED bit is set, and otherwise sets the UPDATED bit in *ctx. If that update step failed it returns 0. Otherwise it returns the result of fake_rsa_dgstvfy_final, which calls fake_rsa_dgstsgnvfy_final with a NULL siglen: that returns 0 if ctx is NULL, the flag byte is 0 or FINALISED is set (these cannot hold after a successful update step), or if the SIGN bit is set (a sign context with no siglen); the VERIFY bit is not required. In the remaining case it sets the FINALISED bit when the NO_DUP bit is set, does not write to sig (the sign branch is skipped because siglen is NULL), and returns 1.

name: qtest_create_quic_connection_ex
prose: Drives a QUIC client SSL (clientssl, may be NULL for server-only) and a QUIC test server (qtserv) until the client has connected or failed with the wanted error and the server has confirmed the handshake or terminated, and returns 1 only if neither side recorded an error; returns 0 otherwise. With thread support (OPENSSL_THREADS and no CRYPTO_TDEBUG) a non-NULL clientssl resets abortserverthread and client_ready under the mutex. It returns 0 immediately if qtserv is NULL. If clientssl is NULL the client side is treated as done (retc = 1). If clientssl is in blocking mode, with thread support it stores qtserv in globtserv, starts run_server_thread (returns 0 if the thread cannot be started), sets qtserv to NULL and treats the server side as done (rets = 1); without thread support it returns 0. The loop then repeatedly: calls SSL_connect (an error equal to wanterr counts as success for the client, setting retc = 1; with a server thread it instead asks the thread to abort via abortserverthread, otherwise it also sets rets = 1 without checking whether the server confirmed the handshake; any error other than WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE sets clienterr), advances the test time, runs SSL_handle_events and the server tick (waiting for client_ready when threaded), polls the server for termination (servererr) or handshake confirmation (rets), and exits through err (returning 0) if both sides have erred, after MAXLOOPS iterations with a non-NULL clientssl, or if qtest_wait_for_timeout fails. After the loop, if a server thread was used and rets > 0, it signals client_ready, waits for the thread, and returns 0 if wait_for_thread or globserverret is false. It returns 1 if clienterr and servererr are both clear, otherwise 0.

Reviewer round 15 and the original rejection (a wanterr error from SSL_connect sets rets = 1 without server confirmation in the non-threaded path, line 585) are right; the old prose said wanterr succeeds only with server confirmation. Tally 2 right.

name: create_bare_ssl_connection_ex
prose: Drives the handshake between a client SSL and a server SSL, both supplied by the caller, until both have completed or something stops it, and returns 1 only when the loop ends because SSL_connect on clientssl and the server step (SSL_accept, or DTLSv1_listen followed by SSL_accept) have both returned > 0. It returns 0 immediately, without writing cm_count or sm_count, if listen is non-zero and serverssl is not DTLS, if BIO_ADDR_new fails, or (in a no-sock build) whenever listen is non-zero. Each loop iteration calls SSL_connect (repeating while the error is WANT_WRITE; an error other than WANT_READ sets clienterr after logging) and then, for the server, either DTLSv1_listen (if listen is still set; a positive return clears listen and continues with SSL_accept in later steps; a negative return is treated as SSL_ERROR_SSL) or SSL_accept (an error other than WANT_READ or WANT_X509_LOOKUP sets servererr). It jumps to the exit, returning 0, if want is not SSL_ERROR_NONE and either side's last error code equals want, if both clienterr and servererr are set, if (for DTLS with read set) an SSL_read that is only meant to trigger retransmits unexpectedly returns > 0, or when abortctr reaches MAXLOOPS; for DTLS it sleeps 50 ms every 10th pass for the first 50. At the exit (after the loop starts) it stores the counts of connect and server-step calls in *cm_count and *sm_count when those pointers are non-NULL and frees the BIO_ADDR. The loop condition is only that retc <= 0 or rets <= 0, so a side that has recorded an error does not by itself end the loop.

Reviewer round 15 (listen path returns 1 after DTLSv1_listen, not SSL_accept) is wrong as stated: a successful DTLSv1_listen sets listen = 0 and rets = 0 (1315-1317) so the loop continues to SSL_accept, and the function only returns 1 at line 1377 when rets > 0; original rejection (the wanted error returns failure) is right: err == want goes to err with ret = 0 (1302-1303, 1338-1339). name: test_hmac_run
prose: Test function with no parameters that exercises the HMAC_CTX API on entries 4, 5 and 6 of the static test table; it returns 1 if all checks pass and 0 at the first failed check. It allocates an HMAC_CTX (returns 0 if that fails) and resets it. It then requires: HMAC_CTX_get_md is NULL, HMAC_Init_ex with NULL key and NULL digest fails, HMAC_Update before init fails, and HMAC_Init_ex with key length -1 and SHA-1 fails. It computes HMAC-SHA1 over test[4] (Init, Update, Final) and compares the hex string with test[4].digest; then requires HMAC_Init_ex with NULL key and SHA-256 to fail (the context was keyed for SHA-1 before); computes HMAC-SHA256 over test[5] (also checking HMAC_CTX_get_md equals EVP_sha256()) and compares with test[5].digest; then initialises with test[6].key and a NULL digest (reusing SHA-256 from the context), updates and finalises over test[6] and compares; and twice more reuses the existing key, once with NULL key and NULL digest and once with NULL key and EVP_sha256(), each over test[6].data and compared with test[6].digest. Each failed check jumps to err, where the context is freed, returning 0; reaching the end returns 1.

name: test_http_method
prose: Test function that runs one mocked HTTP exchange through memory BIOs, selected by do_get (0 means OSSL_HTTP_transfer; non-zero means OSSL_HTTP_get, with do_get > 1 using a "/will-be-redirected" path), do_txt (text/plain request body versus a DER-encoded certificate from the globals x509 and x509_it) and suggested_status (embedded in the request path and consumed by the mock server callback). It builds path, a request BIO req (for do_txt two text strings written to a memory BIO, otherwise ASN1_item_i2d_mem_bio of x509), and the BIOs wbio and rbio; req is set to NULL if the text writes fail. If wbio, rbio or req is NULL it returns 0. It then runs the request (never against the real server, since real_server is always 0) and requires that "suggested_status == HTTP_STATUS_CODES_FATAL_ERROR" has the same truth value as "response is NULL"; if not, it returns 0. When the suggested status is HTTP_STATUS_CODES_FATAL_ERROR (and the response is therefore NULL) it returns 1 without looking at why the response is NULL. Otherwise the response is non-NULL and the result is 1 only if, for do_txt, the first line read from it equals text1, or, for a certificate, d2i_X509_bio yields a certificate that X509_cmp considers equal to x509; the response BIO is freed. At err it frees req, wbio, rbio and the headers stack, and returns res.

name: create_socket
prose: Takes a UDP port number in host byte order (converted with htons) and returns a datagram BIO bound to the IPv6 wildcard address on that port, or NULL on failure. It creates an AF_INET6 SOCK_DGRAM socket with BIO_socket, then, when IPV6_V6ONLY is defined, sets that option to 0 so the socket also accepts IPv4 (failure of setsockopt goes to err); it allocates a BIO_ADDR, fills it with BIO_ADDR_rawmake for AF_INET6 and in6addr_any, binds the fd with BIO_bind, creates the BIO with BIO_new(BIO_s_datagram()) and attaches the fd with BIO_set_fd(sock, fd, BIO_CLOSE) so the BIO owns the descriptor. On success it frees the BIO_ADDR and returns sock. Every failure of those calls prints a message to stderr and goes to err, which frees the BIO_ADDR and the BIO and calls BIO_closesocket(fd) (also when fd is still -1), then returns NULL. Since BIO_set_fd with BIO_CLOSE gives the fd to the BIO, a failure after that point is not possible in this function (the only code after set_fd is the success return).

name: test_tlsext_status_type
prose: Test function with no parameters, using the globals libctx, cert, privkey, ocspcert, cdummyarg, ocsp_client_called and ocsp_server_called, that checks the OCSP status-type settings and callbacks; it returns 1 only if every stage succeeds and 0 otherwise. It returns 0 at once if create_ssl_ctx_pair fails (before the end label, so ocspcert is not touched). Otherwise it checks that the client context's status type is -1 initially, that SSL_new then reports -1, that SSL_set_tlsext_status_type(TLSEXT_STATUSTYPE_ocsp) works on an SSL, and that after setting it on the context new SSLs inherit it. It then installs ocsp_client_cb and ocsp_server_cb with argument &cdummyarg and requires a handshake to succeed with both callbacks having been called (the callbacks set the flags; they were not read here), then resets the flags and cdummyarg to 0 and requires a second handshake to fail with neither flag set, then sets cdummyarg to 2, builds an OCSP_RESPID from the server certificate read from cert (overwriting the global ocspcert with a freshly allocated X509, without freeing any earlier value), hands the stack to the client SSL with SSL_set_tlsext_status_ids (ownership transferred) and requires a third handshake to succeed with both callbacks called. Any failed step jumps to end, which frees the SSL objects, both contexts, any remaining OCSP_RESPID stack and id, the BIO, frees ocspcert and sets it to NULL, and returns testresult (0 unless it reached the final statement).

name: test_early_data_replay_int
prose: Test helper taking idx (passed to setupearly_data_test), usecb (0 no allow-early-data callback, 1 or 2 callback installed) and confopt (when usecb > 0, 0 sets SSL_OP_NO_ANTI_REPLAY directly, otherwise the same through SSL_CONF_cmd "Options" "-AntiReplay"); it resets allow_ed_cb_called to 0 first and uses the globals libctx, cert, privkey, clientpsk and serverpsk. It returns 0 immediately, without freeing or clearing clientpsk and serverpsk, if create_ssl_ctx_pair fails. Otherwise it configures the callback (SSL_CONF_CTX_new failure or a SSL_CONF_cmd result other than 2 goes to end), runs setupearly_data_test, makes a connection that must reuse the session (using up the ticket), shuts down and frees it, creates new SSL objects with the old session, writes early data from the client and checks that SSL_write_early_data wrote all bytes. For usecb <= 1 the server's SSL_read_early_data must return SSL_READ_EARLY_DATA_FINISH with early-data status SSL_EARLY_DATA_REJECTED. For usecb == 2 SSL_read_early_data must return SSL_READ_EARLY_DATA_SUCCESS; if it does not, testresult is set to the return value of check_early_data_timeout(timer) and the function ends there (so it can return 1 on that path); otherwise it checks the data, calls SSL_connect, requires a second SSL_read_early_data to return FINISH with status SSL_EARLY_DATA_ACCEPTED. It then completes the connection and requires SSL_session_reused to be 1 when usecb > 0 (0 otherwise) and allow_ed_cb_called to be 1 when usecb > 0 (0 otherwise). Reaching the end sets testresult = 1. At end (all paths after the first return) it frees sess, clientpsk, serverpsk (setting both globals to NULL), the SSLs and both contexts.

name: virstor_label
prose: gctl handler for the "label" verb: req supplies nargs, hardcode, arg0 (geom name), arg1..arg(nargs-1) (provider names), vir_size and chunk_size; it returns void and reports problems through gctl_error and early return, so some failures leave earlier providers already modified. It returns with an error if nargs < 2, if arg0 is missing, if vir_size or chunk_size is 0, if the providers' sector sizes differ (checked via g_get_sectorsize for each), if no sector size was found, if g_get_mediasize or g_get_sectorsize returns 0 for a provider in the clearing pass, or if g_metadata_clear fails. A provider smaller than the larger of 4 chunks and the map size only gets a gctl_error "Device %s is too small" without returning. It rounds chunk_size up to a multiple of the sector size, rounds the virtual size down (integer division) to a multiple of the chunk size, and if the map byte size (one virstor_map_entry per chunk) is not a multiple of the sector size adds chunks and recomputes the virtual size so the map fits; it prints a warning if the virtual size is below the summed media size. It then opens arg1 (prefixing _PATH_DEV when the name does not start with it; returns an error if open fails), writes a zero-filled allocation map of total_chunks entries in blocks of at most 1 MiB worth of entries (calloc failure or a write error returns after freeing and closing), generates md_id with arc4random, and for each provider fills the metadata (position, provider size, chunk_count reduced by 1 if the last sector would be used, chunk_next, chunk_reserved = 2 * map_chunks and the ALLOCATED and CURRENT flags only for the first provider, provider name only if hardcode), encodes it into a calloc'd sector (the process exits via err(1, ...) if that allocation fails) and stores it with g_metadata_store; a store failure prints a message, calls gctl_error and returns without handling the remaining providers.

Reviewer round 15 (virtual size is not rounded to a multiple of the map size, only to chunk size) is partly right: the virtual size is first truncated to a multiple of the chunk size (229-231) and then increased so the map fits a whole number of sectors (242-252), not a multiple of the map size; so old prose was wrong. Tally 1 right.

name: be_activate
prose: Activates the boot environment named bootenv (relative to the BE root) in handle lbh; temporary selects a one-time activation. It builds be_path with be_root_concat and calls be_exists on it; if be_exists returns non-zero (it fails e.g. when the dataset is missing or its mountpoint is not /), the function returns set_error(lbh, err) for both the temporary and the permanent case. If temporary is true it then returns the result of lzbe_set_boot_device(zpool_get_name(lbh->active_phandle), lzbe_add, be_path) and does not touch bootfs, the previous BE, or origins. If temporary is false: when lbh->bootfs does not start with "-" it calls be_deactivate(lbh, lbh->bootfs, false) and returns -1 if that fails; it sets the pool's bootfs property with zpool_set_prop to be_path (returns -1 on failure); then it loops, opening be_path with zfs_open (returns -1 if that fails), calling be_zfs_promote(zhp, &found_origin) and closing the handle, until found_origin is false; if found_origin is true and the promote returned a non-zero err it returns that err; when the loop leaves with found_origin false and err non-zero it returns -1. Otherwise it returns BE_ERR_SUCCESS. Before the promotion loop fails the bootfs property has already been changed.

Reviewers: original (temporary path only adds boot device, does not set bootfs etc.) right; round 15 (temporary path can also return set_error when be_exists fails) right (1335-1336 precede the temporary branch). name: be_destroy_internal
prose: Destroys the boot environment dataset or snapshot called name (relative to the BE root of lbh, with an optional @snapshot suffix) according to the BE_DESTROY_* flags in options; odestroyer is true when the call is the recursive destruction of an origin snapshot. Error returns go through set_error(lbh, code), which stores the code in lbh->error, optionally prints it, and returns the code itself (a BE_ERR_* value, not -1). Returns BE_ERR_NOENT if the filesystem or snapshot does not exist, BE_ERR_DESTROYACT if the filesystem path equals lbh->rootfs or lbh->bootfs, BE_ERR_ZFSOPEN if zfs_open fails, BE_ERR_NOMEM if strdup of the snapshot name fails, BE_ERR_DESTROYMNT if the filesystem is mounted and BE_DESTROY_FORCE is not set (when it is set the filesystem is unmounted, ignoring the unmount result), and also if be_destroy_cb fails with EBUSY, BE_ERR_UNKNOWN for other be_destroy_cb errors. If the path equals lbh->bootonce it clears the boot-once device with lzbe_set_boot_device. It then calls be_promote_dependent_clones; on error it returns set_error(lbh, err) of that error (for example BE_ERR_HASCLONES), except that when odestroyer is true, the error is BE_ERR_HASCLONES and BE_DESTROY_AUTOORIGIN is set it returns 0 without destroying anything. When BE_DESTROY_WANTORIGIN is set it reads the dataset's origin property, and returns BE_ERR_NOORIGIN if that read fails and BE_DESTROY_ORIGIN is set. If BE_DESTROY_AUTOORIGIN is set and the origin name is an automatic snapshot name it adds BE_DESTROY_ORIGIN. After be_destroy_cb succeeds and the dataset is closed it returns 0 when BE_DESTROY_ORIGIN is not set; otherwise it returns BE_ERR_INVORIGIN if the origin is empty or not longer than root plus one, returns 0 if the origin is not under lbh->root, and otherwise returns the result of the recursive be_destroy_internal on the origin with BE_DESTROY_ORIGIN cleared and odestroyer true. The zfs handle fs is not closed on the DESTROYMNT-unforced, promote-failure and NOORIGIN returns, and the duplicated snapshot name is not freed on the NOORIGIN return.

name: __bt_open
prose: Creates and returns a DB handle for a btree on file fname (an in-memory tree backed by an unlinked temporary file when fname is NULL), or returns NULL with errno set. It copies openinfo (or fills defaults when openinfo is NULL) and fails with EINVAL if openinfo->flags has bits other than R_DUP, if psize is non-zero but below MINPSIZE, above MAX_PAGE_OFFSET + 1 or not indx_t-aligned, if minkeypage is 1, or if lorder is neither BIG_ENDIAN nor LITTLE_ENDIAN after defaulting; it also returns EINVAL for access modes other than O_RDONLY and O_RDWR on a named file (O_RDONLY sets B_RDONLY) and for a non-O_RDWR mode when fname is NULL. It allocates the BTREE and DB (calloc failure returns NULL), sets B_NEEDSWAP when the byte order differs from the machine's, opens the file with flags | O_CLOEXEC (or tmp() with B_INMEM), and fstat()s it. If the file is non-empty it reads a BTMETA; a short read gives EFTYPE, a wrong magic (after byte-swap detection), version, page size outside the allowed range or unknown flags also give EFTYPE; otherwise page size, flags, free list head and record count come from the file. If the file is empty it picks the page size from st_blksize (clamped to MINPSIZE and MAX_PAGE_OFFSET + 1) when none was given, sets B_NODUPS unless R_DUP, bt_free = P_INVALID, nrecs 0 and B_METADIRTY. It rounds the cache size to a multiple of the page size and to at least MINCACHE pages, computes bt_ovflsize, opens the mpool (with __bt_pgin/__bt_pgout filters unless B_INMEM) and calls nroot (failure goes to err). Finally it sets B_DB_LOCK, B_DB_SHMEM and B_DB_TXN from dflags and returns the DB. The err path frees the DB and BTREE and closes the fd if one was opened, but does not close the mpool opened at line 296, so a failure of nroot leaves bt_mp allocated.

name: bt_fast
prose: Fast path for sequential inserts into a btree: tries to place the key at the position remembered from the previous insert (t->bt_last.pgno and t->bt_last.index) without a tree search, and returns &t->bt_cur on a hit or NULL on a miss. It pins the page with mpool_get; if that fails it sets t->bt_order to NOT and returns NULL, leaving bt_cur and *exactp unchanged. Otherwise it stores the page and the remembered index in t->bt_cur (these stay set even on a miss) and treats it as a miss if the free space on the page (upper - lower) is smaller than the space for the new leaf entry plus an index slot. When t->bt_order is FORWARD it is a miss if the page has a next page, if the index is not the last index on the page (NEXTINDEX - 1), or if __bt_cmp of the key against that entry is negative; on a hit it advances t->bt_cur.index by one when the key differs from the entry and records the new index in t->bt_last.index. In the other case (backward order) it is a miss if the page has a previous page, if the index is not 0, or if the key compares greater than the entry; on a hit it sets t->bt_last.index to 0. On a miss it sets t->bt_order to NOT, releases the page with mpool_put and returns NULL (leaving t->bt_cur.page pointing at the released page). On a hit it sets *exactp to 1 when the key compared equal and returns &t->bt_cur with the page still pinned.

name: main
prose: Driver for the DB(3) regression script interpreter: options -f file, -i infoarg, -l (adds DB_LOCK to the open flags), -o file (output file, opened with O_TRUNC) and -s are parsed with getopt; an unknown option calls usage(), an unopenable -o file calls the local err(), and exactly two operands must remain (otherwise usage()), the database type (via dbtype) and a script path, where "-" keeps stdin and any other path is reopened as stdin (err on failure). The -i string is split on commas, tabs and spaces and each non-empty piece is passed to setinfo. The database file is $TMPDIR/__dbtest or /var/tmp/__dbtest when no -f is given (unlinked first), or the -f name (unlinked unless -s); dbopen failure calls err. Script lines are then read with fgets: when the output is stdout the trailing newline is removed, and lines that are empty, begin with a whitespace character or with # are skipped. The first character selects a command (c compare, e echo to the output fd, g get, p put, r remove, S sync, s seq, f set flags, o dump, k/K key text or key file, d/D data text or data file); a command, key or data line seen in the wrong state, a K line for recno, a key or data given to a command that does not take it, or an unknown command character calls err(), as does a short write for echo. The commands then call compare, get, getdata, put, rem, synk, seq or dump on the open DB, with the r and s commands acting immediately on the previous key when the flags are R_CURSOR (for s, otherwise when flags are not R_CURSOR). After end of input it calls dbp->close (err on failure), closes the output fd and calls exit(0); main ends by calling exit(0) or through err()/usage(). The local err() prints "dbtest: " and the message and calls exit(1), so each err() call terminates the process with status 1, usage() also exits with 1; allocated keys/data are freed in most branches but not on every error exit.

name: __xuname
prose: Fills namebuf, treated as five consecutive fields of namesize bytes (sysname, nodename, release, version, machine), and returns 0 or -1. For sysname (UNAME_s), release (UNAME_r), version (UNAME_v) and machine (UNAME_m), if the environment variable is set its value is copied into the field with strlcpy (truncated to namesize - 1 characters and NUL-terminated); otherwise the field is read with sysctl (KERN_OSTYPE, KERN_OSRELEASE, KERN_VERSION, HW_MACHINE) and its last byte is forced to NUL. The nodename field has no environment override and is read with sysctl(KERN_HOSTNAME), last byte forced to NUL. A sysctl failure with errno ENOMEM (output truncated) restores the previous errno and is not counted as an error; any other sysctl failure makes the return value -1 (the remaining fields are still processed). In the sysctl path for the version field, after the sysctl each newline or tab within the first len bytes (len as updated by sysctl, or the original namesize if the call failed) is replaced by a space, except that those within the last two of those bytes are replaced by NUL; this replacement is not done when UNAME_v is set. The function returns 0 if no sysctl call failed with an error other than ENOMEM, and -1 otherwise.

name: __fts_read_44bsd
prose: Returns the next entry of the traversal for FTS stream sp, or NULL. If sp->fts_cur is NULL or FTS_STOP is set it returns NULL immediately without changing errno. Otherwise it takes the current node p = sp->fts_cur, saves its fts_instr and resets it to FTS_NOINSTR. For FTS_AGAIN it re-stats p with fts_stat (no follow) and returns the same node. For FTS_FOLLOW on a node whose fts_info is FTS_SL or FTS_SLNONE it re-stats with following; if the result is FTS_D and FTS_NOCHDIR is not set it opens "." to remember the location (on failure the node gets FTS_ERR and fts_errno, otherwise FTS_SYMFOLLOW is set), and returns the same node. If p is a directory in pre-order (FTS_D) it either marks it FTS_DP and returns it (when the instruction was FTS_SKIP, or FTS_XDEV is set and the device differs from the root's; the symlink fd is closed and any cached child list freed), or descends: it discards a cached name-only child list, changes into the directory for a cached child list (on failure it records fts_errno, sets FTS_DONTCHDIR and rewrites the children's access paths) or builds the child list with fts_build(BREAD) (if that returns NULL it returns NULL when FTS_STOP is set and otherwise returns the directory itself), then returns the first child with the path updated. For any other node it moves to the next sibling (freeing the old node): a sibling at root level triggers a change to the root directory (failure sets FTS_STOP and returns NULL) and fts_load; siblings with instruction FTS_SKIP are skipped and FTS_FOLLOW siblings are stat-followed like above. With no sibling it frees the node and moves to the parent: when the parent is the root parent it frees it, sets errno to 0 and returns NULL with fts_cur NULL (normal end); otherwise it terminates the path, changes back to the parent directory (via the root fd, the saved symlink fd, or "..", setting FTS_STOP and returning NULL, with errno from the failed call, if that fails) and returns the parent with fts_info FTS_ERR if it has a non-zero fts_errno and FTS_DP otherwise. Except in the FTS_AGAIN and FTS_FOLLOW cases, which return without updating the path, sp->fts_cur is set to the returned node.
note: fts-compat.c:307-491 read in full. Reviewers: original (the instruction is consumed by fts_read itself; FTS_AGAIN/FOLLOW return the same node) right, 322-329; round 15 (FTS_FOLLOW re-stats only symlinks; FTS_SKIP gives FTS_DP only for pre-order directories) right, 337-338 and 352-364. Tally 2 right. In the FTS_AGAIN/FOLLOW returns sp->fts_cur already equals p.

name: __fts_children_44bsd
prose: Returns the list of children of the current entry sp->fts_cur (the caller must have a non-NULL fts_cur; the function dereferences it). If instr is neither 0 nor FTS_NAMEONLY it sets errno to EINVAL and returns NULL. Otherwise it sets errno to 0 and returns NULL if FTS_STOP is set; if the current entry's fts_info is FTS_INIT it returns that entry's fts_link (the root list, still owned by the stream); if fts_info is anything other than FTS_D (a directory visited in pre-order) it returns NULL. It then frees any previous sp->fts_child list (the pointer is not cleared before the next assignment), sets the FTS_NAMEONLY flag when instr is FTS_NAMEONLY (reading names only, BNAMES) and otherwise reads with BCHILD, and builds the list with fts_build. When the current entry is not at the root level, its access path is absolute, or FTS_NOCHDIR is set, it stores and returns the fts_build result in sp->fts_child. Otherwise it opens "." first (returns NULL if that fails), builds the list, then restores the directory with fchdir; if the fchdir fails it closes the fd and returns NULL (leaving sp->fts_child set to the built list); otherwise it closes the fd and returns sp->fts_child. fts_build may return NULL for an empty directory or on error, with errno distinguishing the cases only as the callee leaves it.
note: fts-compat.c:513-578 read in full; fts_build not read. Reviewers: round 1 (FTS_INIT path returns p->fts_link) right, 537-538; round 2 (invalid instr returns NULL with EINVAL) right, 518-521; round 15 (fts_info FTS_DNR is only set by fts_build for BREAD, not BCHILD/BNAMES) not checked against fts_build, my prose does not mention it. name: freebsd11_fts_read
prose: FreeBSD 11 ABI version of fts_read: returns the next FTSENT11 for stream sp, or NULL. If sp->fts_cur is NULL or FTS_STOP is set it returns NULL at once without touching errno. Otherwise it takes p = sp->fts_cur, saves its fts_instr and resets it to FTS_NOINSTR. FTS_AGAIN re-stats p (fts_stat without following) and returns the same node; FTS_FOLLOW on a node with fts_info FTS_SL or FTS_SLNONE re-stats it following the link, and if the result is a directory and FTS_NOCHDIR is not set opens "." (on failure sets FTS_ERR and fts_errno, else sets FTS_SYMFOLLOW) and returns the same node. A pre-order directory (FTS_D) is turned into FTS_DP and returned when the instruction was FTS_SKIP or FTS_XDEV is set and the device differs from the root's (closing a symlink fd and freeing any cached child list). Otherwise it drops a name-only child list, then either changes into the directory for an existing child list (on failure recording fts_errno on the directory, setting FTS_DONTCHDIR and fixing the children's access paths) or builds the list with fts_build(BREAD); if that returns NULL it returns NULL when FTS_STOP is set and otherwise returns the directory node itself; with a non-empty list it returns the first child with the path updated. For other nodes it advances to the next sibling (freeing the old node): a sibling at root level triggers fchdir to the root directory (failure sets FTS_STOP, returns NULL without freeing the old node) and fts_load; FTS_SKIP siblings are skipped and FTS_FOLLOW siblings are stat-followed. With no sibling it moves to the parent: at the root-parent level it frees both nodes, sets errno to 0 and returns NULL with fts_cur NULL (normal end of traversal); otherwise it NUL-terminates the path and changes back to the parent (root fd, saved symlink fd, or ".."), setting FTS_STOP and returning NULL with the failing call's errno if that fails, then frees the old node, sets fts_info to FTS_ERR when the parent's fts_errno is non-zero and FTS_DP otherwise, and returns the parent. Except for the FTS_AGAIN and FTS_FOLLOW returns, sp->fts_cur is set to the returned node.

name: fts_stat
prose: Classifies the entry p of stream sp and returns an FTS_* info code; follow selects link handling (0 no, positive follow, negative follow only if the target is a directory) and dfd is -1 (use p->fts_accpath relative to the current directory) or a directory descriptor (use p->fts_name relative to it). The stat result goes into p->fts_statp, or into a local buffer when FTS_NOSTAT is set. If p has FTS_ISW set it returns FTS_W, first zeroing p->fts_statp and setting st_mode to S_IFWHT only when the stat buffer is the entry's own. When FTS_LOGICAL is set or follow is non-zero it calls fstatat following links; if that fails, or if follow < 0 and the target is not a directory, it retries with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW; if the retry fails it stores the first errno in p->fts_errno, zeroes the buffer and returns FTS_NS; otherwise it sets errno to 0 and returns FTS_SLNONE when the first stat failed and the second shows a symlink. Without following it does only the no-follow stat and returns FTS_NS with p->fts_errno set (buffer zeroed) on failure. For a directory it sets p->fts_dev, p->fts_ino and p->fts_nlink (also under FTS_NOSTAT), returns FTS_DOT if the name is ".", scans the ancestors for the same device and inode and returns FTS_DC with p->fts_cycle set to the matching ancestor, and otherwise returns FTS_D. It returns FTS_SL for a symlink, FTS_F for a regular file and FTS_DEFAULT for any other type.

name: fts_read
prose: Returns the next FTSENT for stream sp, or NULL. If sp->fts_cur is NULL or FTS_STOP is set it returns NULL at once without touching errno. Otherwise it takes p = sp->fts_cur, saves its fts_instr and resets it to FTS_NOINSTR. FTS_AGAIN re-stats p (fts_stat without following) and returns the same node; FTS_FOLLOW on a node with fts_info FTS_SL or FTS_SLNONE re-stats it following the link, and if the result is a directory and FTS_NOCHDIR is not set opens "." (on failure sets FTS_ERR and fts_errno, else sets FTS_SYMFOLLOW) and returns the same node. A pre-order directory (FTS_D) is turned into FTS_DP and returned when the instruction was FTS_SKIP or FTS_XDEV is set and the device differs from the root's (closing a symlink fd and freeing any cached child list). Otherwise it drops a name-only child list, then either changes into the directory for an existing child list (on failure recording fts_errno on the directory, setting FTS_DONTCHDIR and fixing the children's access paths) or builds the list with fts_build(BREAD); if that returns NULL it returns NULL when FTS_STOP is set and otherwise returns the directory node itself; with a list it returns the first child with the path updated. For other nodes it advances to the next sibling (freeing the old node): a sibling at root level triggers fchdir to the root directory (failure sets FTS_STOP and returns NULL) and fts_load; FTS_SKIP siblings are skipped and FTS_FOLLOW siblings are stat-followed. With no sibling it moves to the parent: at the root-parent level it frees both nodes, sets errno to 0 and returns NULL with fts_cur NULL (normal end); otherwise it NUL-terminates the path and changes back to the parent (root fd, saved symlink fd, or ".."), setting FTS_STOP and returning NULL with the failing call's errno if that fails, then frees the old node, sets fts_info to FTS_ERR when the parent's fts_errno is non-zero and FTS_DP otherwise, and returns the parent. Except for the FTS_AGAIN and FTS_FOLLOW returns, sp->fts_cur is set to the returned node. The caller must not use a node returned by an earlier call after the next call, since nodes are freed when passed.

name: nfcmp
prose: Compares the name-field string nf with the name field at the start of the record rec, where the name field is taken to end at the first colon (included). It scans rec for the first ':' or NUL; if it reaches the NUL without a colon it returns 1 (not a match) and leaves rec unchanged. Otherwise it saves the byte after the colon, temporarily writes a NUL there, calls strcmp(nf, rec) on the truncated string (so the colon is part of the compared text), restores the saved byte and returns the strcmp result, which is 0 when nf equals the record's text up to and including the first colon and non-zero otherwise. rec is modified only temporarily and holds its original contents when the function returns; the byte after the colon must be writable.

name: _CITRUS_PROP_READ_UINT_COMMON(num, uint64_t, UINT64_MAX)
prose: Generated function _citrus_prop_read_num_common(ms, result, base, neg), a static function created by the _CITRUS_PROP_READ_UINT_COMMON macro with _type_ uint64_t and _max_ UINT64_MAX. It reads characters from the memory stream ms one at a time with _memstream_getc, converting each (upper-cased) character through the xdigit table to a digit value, and accumulates acc = acc * base + digit. It stops at the first character that is not a digit below base, or at the first digit that would make the value exceed UINT64_MAX (checked with cutoff = UINT64_MAX / base and cutlim = UINT64_MAX % base), so the character it stops on may be a non-digit or an overflowing digit. It then pushes back exactly that last character read with _memstream_ungetc, stores acc in *result (negated modulo 2^64, as -acc, when neg is non-zero, otherwise unchanged) and returns 0. It has no error return: overflow ends the number early rather than failing, and base must be non-zero and at most the length of the xdigit table for the digit test to be meaningful.

name: _EUC_mbrtowc_impl
prose: Restartable EUC multibyte-to-wide-character conversion; ps is a conversion state (_EucState) holding the number of bytes still wanted (want) and the partial value (ch), and cs2/cs2width/cs3/cs3width describe the two single-shift code sets. If es->want is negative or greater than MB_CUR_MAX it sets errno to EINVAL and returns (size_t)-1 with the state unchanged. If s is NULL it behaves as if s pointed at "" with n = 1 and pwc = NULL; then if n is 0 it returns (size_t)-2 without changing the state or errno. When es->want is 0 and the first byte has the high bit clear it stores it in *pwc (when pwc is non-NULL) and returns 0 for NUL, otherwise 1, leaving the state unchanged; a first byte >= 0xa1 starts a 2-byte sequence, a byte equal to cs2 or cs3 starts a sequence of cs2width or cs3width bytes, and any other high-bit byte sets errno to EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-1; for a new sequence es->want is set to the wanted length and es->ch to 0. When es->want is non-zero it continues with want = es->want and the saved es->ch (the continuation bytes are not validated). It then shifts up to MIN(want, n) bytes into the value; if fewer than want bytes were available it saves the remaining count in es->want and the partial value in es->ch, sets errno to EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-2. If the sequence is complete it stores the wide character in *pwc when pwc is non-NULL, sets es->want to 0 (es->ch keeps whatever it held, 0 after a sequence that began in this call) and returns 0 if the value is L'\0', otherwise the sequence length want.

name: setlocale
prose: Queries or sets the program locale for category (LC_ALL or one of the individual categories) and returns a pointer to the resulting locale name, or NULL on error. If category is below LC_ALL or at/above _LC_LAST it sets errno to EINVAL and returns NULL. If locale is NULL it returns current_categories[category] for a single category or currentlocale() for LC_ALL, and changes neither the stored categories nor errno. Otherwise it first copies current_categories into new_categories, then fills new_categories from locale: an empty string takes the names from the environment (__get_locale_env) for every category (LC_ALL) or just the one category, returning NULL with EINVAL if a name is longer than ENCODING_LEN; a non-empty string for a single category is copied (EINVAL and NULL if longer than ENCODING_LEN); for LC_ALL a string without '/' is copied to all categories (same length check), and a string with '/' is split into per-category names (EINVAL and NULL if it consists only of slashes or a component is longer than ENCODING_LEN; names beyond the last category are silently ignored, and categories not given are copied from the previous one). For a single category it then returns loadlocale(category). For LC_ALL it loads each category in turn, saving the old name; if loading category i fails it saves errno, reloads the previously loaded categories 1..i-1 from their saved names (falling back to "C" if that also fails), restores errno and returns NULL; if all succeed it returns currentlocale().

name: _nis_gethostbyaddr
prose: nsswitch dispatch method for reverse host lookup through NIS; rval points to a struct hostent * result slot and ap supplies, in order, addr, len, af, hptr, buffer, buflen, errnop and h_errnop. In every build it first stores NULL in *(struct hostent **)rval. Without YP defined it returns NS_UNAVAIL at once (the NULL stays in the slot). With YP defined it reads the arguments, gets the thread's resolver state, and if __hostent_data_init returns NULL sets the resolver h_errno to NETDB_INTERNAL, stores it in *h_errnop and returns NS_NOTFOUND. It then calls _gethostbynisaddr_r (which formats addr with inet_ntop, returning -1 if that fails, and otherwise looks it up in the hosts.byaddr map for AF_INET or ipnodes.byaddr for other families); if that returns non-zero it stores the current resolver h_errno in *h_errnop and returns NS_NOTFOUND (errnop untouched). If __copy_hostent into hptr and buffer fails it stores errno in *errnop, sets the resolver h_errno to NETDB_INTERNAL, stores it in *h_errnop and returns NS_RETURN with the result slot still NULL. Otherwise it stores hptr in the result slot and returns NS_SUCCESS.

name: link_ntoa_r
prose: Formats the link-level address of sdl as text into obuf (obuf may be NULL; sdl and buflen must be non-NULL, asserted) and reports the space needed through *buflen. The text is the interface name (sdl_nlen bytes, capped at IFNAMSIZ, copied as is), then a ':' only if the name length is greater than 0 and sdl_alen > 0, then each address byte in lowercase hexadecimal, a byte above 0xf as two digits and a byte up to 0xf as one digit without a leading zero, with '.' between bytes. Output is written only while it fits: each piece is checked to leave room for one more byte for the terminating NUL, and once a piece does not fit nothing more is written (rem set to 0, later pieces are skipped even if they would fit). When obuf is non-NULL and the initial *buflen was non-zero it always writes a NUL at the current output position, which is inside the buffer because earlier pieces were only written when room for the NUL remained. *buflen is then set to the total length needed including the NUL (the count stops growing if it would exceed SIZE_MAX). The function returns 0 if obuf was non-NULL, the initial *buflen was positive and every piece fit, and -1 otherwise (including when obuf is NULL, *buflen is 0, or the text was truncated). The initial *buflen is stored in an int.

name: _nsdispatch
prose: Name-service dispatcher: for the database and method_name it tries the configured sources in order (or the NULL-name terminated defaults list when the database has no configured entry), passing the variadic arguments to each source's method, and returns an NS_* result; errno is saved on entry and restored to that value on every return path (the label fin). If the process is threaded it takes the nss_lock read lock; if that fails it returns NS_UNAVAIL (lock not held). It then calls fb_getstate and nss_configure; if either returns non-zero it returns NS_UNAVAIL while the read lock, if it was taken, is still held and without having incremented dispatch_depth. Otherwise it increments the dispatch depth and, when that exceeds the fallback depth, looks up the database's source list and the fallback method. For each source in the list it sets result to NS_NOTFOUND and looks up the method; if one exists it clears errno, calls it (with NS_CACHING compiled in, a "cache" source is handled through the cache read functions, may be skipped when issetugid() is non-zero under NS_STRICT_LIBC_EID_CHECKING, and a later cache write is done for NS_SUCCESS or NS_NOTFOUND results) and stops the loop when the result intersects that source's flags; a result that does not match the flags goes on to the next source. If no method exists, the fallback method (if any) is called with the source name and its result becomes the source's result; the loop does not stop on a fallback result because it is not checked against the flags; with no fallback the source gives NS_NOTFOUND after a debug log. The function returns the result from the last source tried (the matching one, or the last one if none matched); if the source list is empty it returns the 0 from nss_configure. Normal exit releases the read lock when threaded and decrements dispatch_depth.

name: acl_strip_np
prose: Returns a newly allocated ACL holding only the trivial entries of aclp, chosen by the brand of aclp (aclp must be a valid acl_t; _acl_brand is called on it), or NULL with errno set. For ACL_BRAND_NFS4 it calls _nfs4_acl_strip_np(aclp, 0), which allocates a new NFS4-branded ACL with acl_init (ENOMEM and NULL if that fails), derives a mode from aclp with acl_nfs4_sync_mode_from_acl and fills the new ACL with acl_nfs4_trivial_from_mode_libc; recalculate_mask is ignored for this brand. For ACL_BRAND_POSIX it calls _posix1e_acl_strip_np(aclp, recalculate_mask), which duplicates aclp with acl_dup (NULL if that fails), allocates a new ACL (NULL, after freeing the duplicate, if that fails), copies the ACL_USER_OBJ, ACL_GROUP_OBJ and ACL_OTHER entries into it while walking the duplicate with acl_get_entry (the walk simply ends if acl_get_entry stops returning 1, including on an error, and the partial result is then returned), notes whether an ACL_MASK entry existed, and if one existed and recalculate_mask is non-zero calls acl_calc_mask. If acl_get_tag_type, acl_create_entry, acl_copy_entry or acl_calc_mask fails it frees both ACLs and returns NULL, with errno as left by the failing call. On the success path of the POSIX case the duplicate acl_old is not freed. For any other brand it sets errno to EINVAL and returns NULL.

name: __signalcontext
prose: PowerPC64 helper that rewrites the context ucp so that resuming it runs func(sig, siginfo, ucontext) through ctx_wrapper on a fresh frame; it returns 0. If ucp is NULL it calls abort(). It takes the saved stack pointer ucp->uc_mcontext.mc_gpr[1], subtracts sizeof(ucontext_t), aligns down to 16 bytes and copies *ucp (the original context, before it is modified) there as sig_uc; it then subtracts sizeof(siginfo_t), aligns again, zero-fills the siginfo_t there with bzero and sets si_signo to sig; it subtracts a further 48 bytes (6 * sizeof(uint64_t)) for a frame pointer area and aligns the resulting stack pointer down to 16 bytes. It then zeroes ucp->uc_mcontext, sets ucp->uc_link to the copied context sig_uc, removes sig from ucp->uc_sigmask with sigdelset, and fills in the mcontext: version _MC_VERSION, length, mc_srr0 = ctx_wrapper, mc_gpr[1] = the new stack pointer, mc_gpr[3] = func, mc_gpr[4] = sig, mc_gpr[5] = the siginfo pointer and mc_gpr[6] = sig_uc. The stack below the saved stack pointer must have room for the two structures and the 48 bytes; nothing checks this.

name: walk
prose: Core matcher step loop of the regex engine, used in two modes selected by fast; it runs the state set through the subject from start toward stop using step(), starting at strip state startst with stopst as the accepting state. It begins with the state set containing startst (after one NOTHING step); in fast mode it also saves that set as the fresh state. At each position it decodes the next character with XMBRTOWC (the end of subject gives OUT with length 0), applies the BOL/EOL, beginning/end-of-string and word-boundary steps that apply between the previous and current character, then tests whether stopst is in the set: in fast mode that ends the loop, in slow mode it records matchp = p and continues. The loop also ends when the state set is empty, when p equals stop, or when the character length exceeds the remaining bytes; otherwise it steps over the character (fast mode restarts from the fresh state at each position, slow mode from an empty set) and advances p. In fast mode, matchp is set to p whenever the state set equals the fresh set at the top of an iteration; at exit it sets m->coldp to matchp and returns p advanced by the length XMBRTOWC reports for the character at p (at least 1, because that helper returns 1 for NUL and for invalid sequences) if stopst is in the set, and NULL otherwise. In slow mode it returns matchp, the last position at which stopst was in the set, or NULL if there was none, and does not change m->coldp.

name: regress
prose: Reads regression-test lines from the open stream in and runs them through try(), then runs five regerror() self-checks; it returns no value and reports failures through the global status and stderr. For each line read with fgets (buffer of 1000 bytes) it first increments the global line counter, so skipped lines are counted too, and skips lines whose first character is '#' or a newline. For other lines it overwrites the last character of the line with NUL (the newline, or the last character if the line was truncated or lacked a newline), prints the line number if debug is set, splits the line with split() into at most 10 fields on tabs, and if there are fewer than 3 fields prints "bad input, line N" and calls exit(1). Fields equal to the two characters "" become empty strings; fields 3 and 4 are set to NULL when absent. It calls try() with the first five fields and the options from the second field; when the second field contains '&' it calls try() a second time with REG_EXTENDED cleared. After end of input it checks regerror(REG_BADPAT) into a 100-byte buffer for the text "invalid regular expression" and its length, a 10-byte truncated version, the REG_ITOA form ("REG_BADPAT") and the REG_ATOI form (a number equal to REG_BADPAT and a consistent length); each failed check prints a message to stderr and sets status to 1.

name: findmust
prose: Computes the "must" string of a compiled regex: the longest run of literal characters (OCHAR operators) that every match must contain, recording it in g->must with its length g->mlen and its offset g->moffset (-1 when the offset is unknown), for use as a quick pre-search. It returns without changing anything if p->error is non-zero, or if MB_CUR_MAX > 1 and the current encoding is not "UTF-8". Otherwise it scans g->strip from element 1 to the OEND element, building runs of OCHAR operators (a wcrtomb failure falls into the "too hard" case) and updating the best run, the mlen and an offset estimate at each operator that breaks a run; alternation/optional constructs are skipped, and if the skip walk meets an element that is not one of the expected branch operators it sets BAD in g->iflags and returns immediately (g->mlen and g->moffset may already be partly updated, g->must untouched). If no OCHAR run was found (g->mlen == 0) it sets g->moffset to -1 and returns. Otherwise it mallocs mlen + 1 bytes for g->must (not freeing any earlier value of g->must, so a non-NULL g->must would be leaked); if malloc fails it sets g->mlen to 0 and g->moffset to -1 and returns; if it succeeds it re-encodes the characters of the chosen run into g->must with wcrtomb and terminates the string with NUL.
